hypotheses: Positive integer width d and epsilon > 0.
A nonempty row of N visible keys.
Keys and arbitrary rotary angles stay fixed while the projected query before RMS varies.
The fixed real gain gamma may equal m*log(N)*g for the implemented SSMax coefficient m and original head gain g.
probability_row_bound: sum_j abs(p_j(q)-p_j(q2)) <= 4*C*norm(q-q2). The factor 4 is conservative, inherited from the existing checked softmax theorem, not claimed sharp.
ssmax_specialization: For m>=0 and N>=1, C=m*log(N)*abs(g)*sqrt(d)/sqrt(epsilon). Ideal original gain g=1/sqrt(d) cancels sqrt(d). Half and quarter multiply both displayed constants by 1/2 and 1/4 relative to the same parent.
nonvacuity: All four statements have examples. The normalized examples use width 8, epsilon 1/8388608, nonzero angles, arbitrary projected vectors, and a four-key row with nonzero gain.
mapping: Uses actual GPTMini.rmsNormEps, SequenceModel.rotateHead and Perspective.softmaxWeight; the real equation matches the visible-key softmax row. PyTorch-to-Lean translation is reviewed, not formally verified.
limitations: No control of unbounded query projection matrices before the measured input.
The query-only theorem holds keys and rotations fixed; it does not bound simultaneous changes to all token projections or learned frequencies.
No bound on value changes, XSA, readout, the whole transformer or training Jacobians.
No floating-point or learning guarantee. Small epsilon still permits large sensitivity constants.
Smaller m weakens the separate conditional concentration bound for a fixed original margin.
preservation: Supplemental analysis of the unchanged model. No scientific Python, plans, original proof records, selected configuration or frozen selection-integrity manifest changed.
